propositions: RemoteRef.instance field is never populated in production code; it is only constructed in tests, making deployment identity unobservable
RemoteRef.instance is derived from the configured base URL and injected at Backend construction time via the build_backend factories, not resolved at call time

The docstring claim that instance prevents same-vendor collision is incorrect; vendor already separates Cloud from DC, and local-id collision between two same-vendor deployments cannot be fixed by instance since _jira_key_to_local_id derives ids from Jira keys alone

Both concrete backends implement remote_ref() port member returning a RemoteRef whose instance is the value explicitly passed at construction, provable by contract tests with no ambient config context
Two backends configured at different base URLs produce unequal RemoteRef objects; equivalent URL spellings (trailing slash, case, default port) produce equal instances
